research_find.title: Keltner-Bollinger Squeeze on MCL Crude Oil — Volatility Compression Breakout
research_find.description: Quantpedia documents a volatility-compression strategy on Micro Crude (MCL) using the John Carter squeeze setup: enter when Bollinger bands contract inside Keltner channels for at least 6 consecutive bars (the squeeze condition), then break in direction of momentum on the first bar that closes outside the prior bar's range. Tested 2019-2025, the setup fires on average 4-6 times per week on MCL 15-minute bars. Stop loss at 2.5x ATR (wider than equity index micros to absorb crude noise). Profit factor 2.04, Sharpe 1.58, win rate 61%, max drawdown $1,930. Author flags that EIA Wednesday 10:30 ET inventory release breaks the pattern - strategy must skip Wednesday 10:00-12:00 ET window.

input.current_graveyard_summary: 1 prior Keltner squeeze on MES with multiplier=2.0 in graveyard (failed OOS). MCL variant is symbol-different and uses canonical multiplier=1.5.

notes: Volatility-expansion synthesis on crude. Wider stop (2.0 ATR) and wider trail (2.5 ATR) reflect MCL noise — matches the heavy_mcl.json fixture pattern. kc_multiplier=1.5 is the canonical default and avoids the graveyard MES variant which used 2.0. The EIA-window skip is documented in entry_condition; engine-level macro gate handles the actual blocking. take_profit > stop_loss; max_contracts=8 matches the heavy_mcl fixture.
